title: THE ADMINISTRATORS-GENERAL ACT, 1963
long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the office and duties of Administrators-General.

sections.section_title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Administrators-General Act, 1963. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.

sections.section_title: Definitions
sections.text: Defines "assets" (a deceased person's movable and immovable property chargeable with debts/legacies or available for distribution), "letters of administration" (general, with will annexed, or limited), "next-of-kin" (including a widow/widower or any person entitled to letters of administration in preference to a creditor/legatee), and "prescribed" (prescribed by rules under this Act).

sections.section_title: Appointment of Administrator-General
sections.text: (1) The State Government shall appoint an Administrator-General for the State, and the same person may be appointed for two or more States. (2) A person is eligible only if he has been, for at least seven years, an advocate or attorney of a High Court; or for ten years a member of the judicial service of a State; or for five years a Deputy Administrator-General.

sections.section_title: Appointment and powers of Deputy Administrator-General
sections.text: (1) The State Government may appoint one or more Deputies to assist the Administrator-General; a Deputy, subject to the Administrator-General's and State Government's control, may discharge any of the Administrator-General's duties and powers, with the same privileges and liabilities. (2) A Deputy must have been, for at least three years, an advocate, attorney of a High Court, or member of the judicial service of a State.

sections.section_title: Incorporation
sections.text: The Administrator-General is a corporation sole with perpetual succession and an official seal, and may sue and be sued in his corporate name.

chapters.chapter_title: RIGHTS, POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE ADMINISTRATOR-GENERAL (a) Grant of letters of administration and probate

sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of High Court for the whole State
sections.text: The High Court is deemed a court of competent jurisdiction to grant probate or letters of administration to the Administrator-General wherever in the State the estate is situate, without affecting any district court's jurisdiction.

sections.section_title: Administrator-General entitled to letters of administration, unless granted to next-of-kin
sections.text: Letters of administration granted by the High Court go to the Administrator-General unless granted to the deceased's next-of-kin.

sections.section_title: Administrator-General entitled to letters of administration in preference to creditors, certain legatees or friends
sections.text: The Administrator-General has a right to letters of administration (other than pendente lite) in preference to a creditor, a non-residuary/non-universal legatee, or a friend of the deceased.

sections.section_title: Right of Administrator-General to apply for administration of estates
sections.text: (1) Where a person dies leaving assets exceeding rupees ten lakhs in a State, and no one applies for probate/letters of administration (or takes other protective proceedings, where not obligatory) within one month of death, the Administrator-General may, within a reasonable time and subject to State rules, take proceedings to obtain letters of administration. (2) He shall do so only if satisfied there is apprehension of misappropriation, deterioration or waste, or that proceedings are otherwise necessary to protect the assets.

sections.section_title: Power of Administrator-General to collect and hold assets where immediate action is required
sections.text: (1) Where assets exceeding rupees ten lakhs face imminent danger of misappropriation, deterioration or waste, the High Court may, on application, direct the Administrator-General to collect and hold, deposit, realise, sell or invest such assets per the Court's directions or, absent directions, per this Act. (2) Such an order entitles the Administrator-General to sue for recovery of the assets, apply for letters of administration, retain prescribed fees, and reimburse himself for lawful payments.

sections.section_title: Grant of probate or letters of administration to person appearing in the course of proceedings taken by Administrator-General
sections.text: Where, during proceedings under section 9 or 10, a claimant establishes a right to probate or letters of administration as next-of-kin (with required security), or shows he is diligently pursuing other protective proceedings (where not obligatory), or the High Court is satisfied there is no apprehension of loss and the grant is unnecessary, the High Court shall grant probate/letters accordingly or drop the proceedings, and in all cases award the Administrator-General his costs from the estate.

sections.section_title: Grant of administration to Administrator-General in certain cases
sections.text: If, within a reasonable period, no valid claimant appears or no due-diligence protective proceedings are shown, and the High Court is satisfied of apprehended loss or necessity, or a claimant fails to give required security, the High Court may grant letters of administration to the Administrator-General.

sections.section_title: Administrator-General not precluded from applying for letters within one month after death
sections.text: The Administrator-General may apply for letters of administration at any time, including within one month of death. (b) Revocation of grants

sections.section_title: Recall of Administrator-General's administration and grant of probate, etc., to executor or next-of-kin
sections.text: Where an executor or next-of-kin not duly served with citation later establishes a preferential claim, letters granted to the Administrator-General shall be revoked (mandatorily if a will is proved; otherwise on timely application within six months without unreasonable delay), and probate/letters granted to the executor/next-of-kin instead.

sections.section_title: Cost of obtaining administration, etc., may, on revocation, be ordered to be paid to Administrator-General out of estate
sections.text: On revocation, the High Court may order the Administrator-General's costs of obtaining and losing the letters, plus fees, to be paid to or retained by him from the estate, subject to section 10(2)(c)-(d).

sections.section_title: After revocation letters granted to Administrator-General to be deemed, as to him, to have been voidable only
sections.text: Revoked letters are deemed voidable, not void, as to the Administrator-General and those acting under his authority, except for acts done after notice of a will or voiding fact, unless proceedings to prove the will or revoke the letters are promptly commenced and diligently prosecuted within one month of such notice.

sections.section_title: Payments made by Administrator-General prior to revocation
sections.text: Payments and acts made by the Administrator-General before revocation (upon grant of probate or letters with will annexed) remain valid despite the revocation, if they would have been valid under such a grant. (c) General

sections.section_title: Administrator-General's petition for grant of letters of administration
sections.text: The Administrator-General's petition need only state the time and place of death, surviving next-of-kin's names/addresses if known, particulars and value of assets, and known liabilities.

sections.section_title: Name in which probate or letters to be granted
sections.text: Probate or letters of administration to an Administrator-General are granted in that official name.

sections.section_title: Effect of probate or letters granted to Administrator-General
sections.text: (1) Probate/letters granted to an Administrator-General have effect over all the deceased's assets throughout India, are conclusive as to representative title against debtors and asset-holders, and indemnify those who pay debts or deliver assets to him. (2) The granting High Court shall certify the grant to High Courts of other States, to be filed there. (3) Certain pre-1968 Jammu and Kashmir grants are deemed as effective as if granted under this section. 21. [Omitted.]―Omitted by the Central Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1968.

sections.section_title: Transfer by private executor or administrator of interest under probate or letters
sections.text: (1) A private executor/administrator may, with the Administrator-General's consent and by a gazetted instrument, transfer estate assets vested in him to the Administrator-General. (2) From the transfer date, the transferor is exempt from liability for future acts, and the Administrator-General assumes the corresponding rights and liabilities as if originally granted the probate/letters.

sections.section_title: Distribution of assets
sections.text: (1) After the prescribed notice period to creditors and others expires, the Administrator-General may distribute assets to satisfy claims of which he has notice. (2) He is not liable for distributed assets to claimants of whom he had no notice. (3) Claims rejected or disallowed in part do not affect him unless enforcement proceedings begin within one month of notice of rejection and are diligently prosecuted. (4) This does not prejudice a claimant's right to follow assets into the hands of recipients. (5) The period between claim submission and the Administrator-General's final decision is excluded from limitation computations.

sections.section_title: Appointment of Official Trustee as trustee of assets after completion of administration
sections.text: (1) Once liabilities of an estate are discharged, the Administrator-General may, after gazette notification and with the Official Trustee's consent, appoint the Official Trustee as trustee of remaining assets, subject to State rules. (2) Such assets then vest in the Official Trustee as if appointed under the Official Trustees Act, 1913, held on the same trusts as before.

sections.section_title: Power of High Court to give directions regarding administration of estate
sections.text: The High Court may, on application, give the Administrator-General general or special directions regarding any estate in his charge.

sections.section_title: No security to be required from Administrator-General
sections.text: No court shall require the Administrator-General to furnish an administration bond or other security on grant of letters of administration.

sections.section_title: Manner in which petition to be verified by Administrator-General
sections.text: The Administrator-General need only verify his petitions by signature; petitions on facts outside his personal knowledge may be verified by a competent person.

sections.section_title: Entry of Administrator-General not to constitute notice of a trust
sections.text: Entry of the Administrator-General's name in a company's books, or dealing with him, does not itself constitute notice of a trust, and a company cannot object to registering his name merely because he is a corporation.

sections.section_title: In what cases Administrator-General may grant certificate
sections.text: (1) Where a deceased's assets in a State (excluding certain savings bank/provident fund sums) did not exceed rupees ten lakhs at death, the Administrator-General may grant a non-creditor claimant a certificate entitling him to receive assets up to that value. (2) No certificate shall be granted before one month from death unless the executor, widow or other entitled person requests it in writing and the Administrator-General thinks fit. (3) No certificate shall be granted where probate/letters of administration have already been granted, or in respect of certain Government Savings Bank/provident fund sums. [State Amendment - Uttar Pradesh: substitutes "ten lakhs rupees" for "two lakhs rupees" in section 29(1).]

sections.section_title: Grant of certificate to creditors and power to take charge of certain estates
sections.text: (1) If no non-creditor claimant obtains a certificate, probate or letters within three months of death, the Administrator-General may administer the estate without letters, as if letters had been granted. (2) If he neglects or refuses to do so, he must, on a creditor's application, grant the creditor a certificate with the same effect as one under section 29. (3) He may require the creditor to give reasonable security before granting such a certificate.

sections.section_title: Administrator-General not bound to grant certificate unless satisfied of claimant's title, etc
sections.text: The Administrator-General need not grant a certificate under section 29 or 30 unless satisfied, after due inquiry, of the claimant's title and the value of the deceased's assets.

sections.section_title: Effect of certificate
sections.text: A certificate holder has the same powers, duties and liabilities regarding the specified assets as if letters of administration had been granted, but need not file accounts/inventories before any authority or (save under section 30) give an administration bond.

sections.section_title: Revocation of certificate
sections.text: (1) The Administrator-General may revoke a certificate obtained by fraud or misrepresentation, or by an untrue allegation of an essential fact (even if made in ignorance or inadvertently). (2) Revocation requires giving the holder a reasonable opportunity to show cause.

sections.section_title: Surrender of revoked certificate
sections.text: (1) On revocation, the holder must surrender the certificate on requisition, without fee refund. (2) Wilful, unreasonable failure to surrender is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

sections.section_title: Payment to holder of certificate before it is revoked
sections.text: Payments made in good faith to a certificate holder before revocation remain a valid discharge to the payer, and the holder may retain/reimburse himself for lawful payments made.

sections.section_title: Administrator-General not bound to take out administration on account of assets for which he has granted certificate
sections.text: The Administrator-General need not take out letters of administration for assets covered by a certificate, unless the certificate is later revoked or the estate's value is found to exceed rupees ten lakhs.

sections.section_title: Transfer of certain assets to executor or administrator in country of domicile for distribution
sections.text: Where a non-domiciled deceased leaves assets in a State and in his domicile country, and administration has been taken there and here, the certificate holder or Administrator-General may, after settling known local claims, transfer the surplus/residue to the domicile-country executor/administrator (with consent) for distribution to persons abroad, instead of distributing it himself.

sections.section_title: Liability of Government
sections.text: The Government must make good sums the Administrator-General would be personally liable for as a private administrator, except liabilities neither he nor his officers contributed to or could have averted by reasonable diligence, in which case neither he nor the Government is liable.

sections.section_title: Creditor's suit against Administrator-General
sections.text: (1) A creditor suing the Administrator-General must pay costs unless he shows he applied in writing, with evidence, at least one month before suing. (2) A decree in the creditor's favour, unless he is secured, entitles him only to rateable payment with other creditors from the estate.

sections.section_title: Notice of suit not required in certain cases
sections.text: Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 does not apply to a suit against the Administrator-General claiming no personal relief against him.

sections.section_title: Fees
sections.text: (1) Prescribed fees (by percentage or otherwise) shall be charged by the State Government for the Administrator-General's duties. (2) Fees may vary by estate/class/duty and shall be set to cover salaries and expenses of administering this Act, including any Government-insurance sum determined necessary.

sections.section_title: Disposal of fees
sections.text: (1) Expenses a private administrator could retain/pay are retained/paid similarly, with prescribed fees retained or paid in addition. (2) The Administrator-General shall remit all fees received to the prescribed authority, credited to Government account.

sections.section_title: Audit
sections.text: Accounts shall be audited at least annually, and at other times if directed, by the prescribed person and manner.

sections.section_title: Auditors to examine accounts and report to Government
sections.text: Auditors shall report to the State Government in the prescribed form, certifying whether accounts were properly audited, complete, whether required books were kept, and whether assets/securities were properly kept/invested/deposited, noting any deficiencies or non-compliance.

sections.section_title: Power of auditors to summon and examine witnesses, and to call for documents
sections.text: (1) Auditors have civil-court powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to summon and examine witnesses on oath, order discovery/inspection, compel document production, and issue commissions for witness examination. (2) Refusal or neglect to comply is an offence under section 188 of the Indian Penal Code, reportable to the State Government.

sections.section_title: Costs of audit, etc
sections.text: Audit costs are determined and defrayed as prescribed by State Government rules.

sections.section_title: General powers of administration
sections.text: The Administrator-General may incur expenditure necessary for proper care and management of estate property, and, with High Court sanction, on reasonable religious, charitable or other objects and improvements.

sections.section_title: Power to summon and examine witnesses
sections.text: (1) The Administrator-General has the same civil-court powers as auditors under section 45(1) to summon and examine witnesses, order discovery/inspection, compel documents, and issue commissions. (2) Section 45(2) applies correspondingly to persons summoned under this section.

sections.section_title: Power of person beneficially interested to inspect Administrator-General's account, etc., and take copies
sections.text: An interested person may, subject to prescribed conditions, inspect estate accounts and auditors' reports/certificates, and obtain copies/extracts on payment of the prescribed fee.

sections.section_title: False evidence
sections.text: A false statement made on oath during an examination under this Act is deemed intentionally false evidence in a stage of judicial proceedings.

sections.section_title: Assets unclaimed for twelve years to be transferred to Government
sections.text: Assets held by the Administrator-General for twelve years or more without a granted payment application shall be transferred to Government account, unless a suit or proceeding regarding them is pending.

sections.section_title: Mode of proceeding by claimant to recover principal money so transferred
sections.text: (1) If a later claim to transferred assets is established to the prescribed authority's satisfaction, the State Government shall pay the claimant the transferred principal (or the due portion). (2) If not so established, the claimant may petition the High Court against the State Government, which, after taking evidence, shall order payment as it thinks fit, binding on all parties. (3) The High Court may direct payment of costs by either party.

sections.section_title: Succession Act or Companies Act not to affect Administrator-General
sections.text: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 and the Companies Act, 1956 do not supersede or affect the Administrator-General's rights, duties and privileges.

sections.section_title: Savings of provisions of Police Acts for presidency-towns
sections.text: Nothing in the Indian Succession Act, 1925 or this Act affects laws on police custody of a deceased intestate's movable property under four hundred rupees in presidency-towns.

sections.section_title: Order of court to be equivalent to decree
sections.text: Any court order under this Act has the same effect as a decree.

sections.section_title: Provision for administration by Consular Officer in case of death in certain circumstances of foreign subject
sections.text: The Central Government may direct that, where a foreign subject dies in India and no one but the Administrator-General is entitled to apply for letters of administration, letters may be granted to a Consular Officer of that foreign State on application, on terms the Court thinks fit subject to Central Government rules.

sections.section_title: Letters of administration not necessary in respects of small estates administered by Administrator-General in accordance with certain Acts
sections.text: The Administrator-General need not take out letters of administration for an estate valued at or below two thousand rupees administered under the Army and Air Force (Disposal of Private Property) Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957, but has the same powers as if letters had been granted.

sections.section_title: Powers to grant Administrator-General letters limited for purpose of dealing with assets in accordance with the Army and Air Force (Disposal of Private Property) Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957
sections.text: On application under those Acts, the Court may grant the Administrator-General letters of administration limited to dealing with the estate under those Acts.

sections.section_title: Act not to affect Army and Air Force (Disposal of Private Property) Act, 1950, or the Navy Act, 1957
sections.text: This Act does not affect the provisions of those Acts.

sections.section_title: Saving of provisions of Indian Registration Act, 1908
sections.text: This Act does not affect the Indian Registration Act, 1908.

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
sections.text: The Central Government may make rules on terms and conditions for granting letters of administration to Consular Officers under section 56.

sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
sections.text: (1) The State Government may make rules to carry out this Act and regulate the Administrator-General's proceedings. (2) Such rules may cover accounts and their audit/inspection; safe custody, deposit and investment of assets/securities; remittance of funds; fees and their collection; statements/schedules to be submitted and published; cost recovery for such documents; determination and defrayal of audit costs; service of summonses and related expenses; and other prescribed matters. (3) Every State Government rule shall be laid before the State Legislature.

sections.section_title: Laying of rules made by Central Government before Parliament
sections.text: Every Central Government rule shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament for thirty days, subject to modification or annulment by Parliament, without prejudice to things already done.

sections.section_title: Repeal and savings
sections.text: (1) The Administrators-General's Act, 1913 is repealed. (2) The repeal does not affect the incorporation of a person holding the office of Administrator-General at commencement, without prejudice to the General Clauses Act, 1897. (3) Section 59B of the Administrators-General's Act, 1913 continues to apply notwithstanding the repeal.
